name: Hollander Electric Co LLC
what_they_do: Master-licensed electrical contractor in business since 1988, based in East Brunswick and serving Milltown and about 30 other central Jersey towns. Commercial and industrial electrical work is the stated primary focus (service upgrades, three-phase distribution, switchgear, motor controls, lighting, standby power, EV charging), with residential electrical and commercial HVAC as secondary offers.
customers: Businesses, facilities and property managers (commercial/industrial) plus homeowners; 24/7 emergency response advertised for commercial and industrial clients.

size_signals.signal: Four licences published sitewide: NJ Master Electrician #9674, Master HVAC #4711 and #6091, HIC #13VH02466500
4.8 rating from 207 Google reviews, with owner replies on reviews
In business since 1988 (stated on site and in profile)

website_review.online_booking_or_quote: quote request form (name, phone, service dropdown, project details) — no scheduling or booking
website_review.trust_signals: Licence numbers in the top bar and repeated in each section, 'since 1988', Google Maps place link, van photo
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Every page's <title> carries no readable text beyond a single emoji character — the site returns '🐴' as the title on the home page and on /electrician/milltown, so search results and AI answers get no title text; no meta description; the big number counters render as '0' until JS animates them
website_review.search_basics: Strong structure — town landing pages and named service sections — but titles/meta are effectively empty, so the good structure is invisible in results
top_issues: Page titles contain no service/town text sitewide; no meta description
No LocalBusiness JSON-LD anywhere despite full licence and address data on page
No booking/scheduling for service calls; quote only

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: claimed, complete, active profile (hours, photos added by owner, 207 reviews, owner replies) and robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Allow: /'. Answerable: lots of readable service text, licences and towns, but zero JSON-LD and no real page title, so the machine-readable layer is missing. Bookable: a labelled quote form (name, phone, service select) with no CAPTCHA and a real submit button, but no calendar booking for a service call.

operations_signals.signal: 24/7 emergency response advertised for commercial and industrial clients, i.e. after-hours calls are part of the product
Owner personally replies to Google reviews (visible owner responses) — ongoing manual review work
Quote form asks only for name, phone and 'project details', so every serious lead needs a callback to scope the job

top_opportunities.opportunity: Fix titles, meta descriptions and add LocalBusiness/ElectricalContractor JSON-LD with the licence numbers, address and hours across all 31 town pages
top_opportunities.evidence: document.title returned only an emoji character on both the home page and /electrician/milltown; 0 JSON-LD scripts; no meta description

top_opportunities.opportunity: Service-call scheduling (not just a quote form) so commercial facilities and homeowners can pick a slot online
top_opportunities.evidence: Only intake is a 3-field quote form plus phone; CTA is 'Request a Quote' on every page

top_opportunities.opportunity: After-hours AI intake for the 24/7 emergency line: triage the call, capture site/panel details, dispatch or schedule
top_opportunities.evidence: Site advertises 24/7 emergency industrial response while the only web channel is a form reviewed during business hours

scores.reasons: Gap 3: the site is well built, but titles, schema and booking are all missing. Ability 5: commercial/industrial electrical with master licences, 207 reviews, decades in business. Ease 5: the title/schema fix is a day's work on an existing, well-structured site. Evidence 5: DOM, robots.txt, titles and the Google profile were all inspected directly.

wrong_claims.claim: Page titles carry a single emoji character as their only text ('document.title returned only an emoji')
wrong_claims.what_is_true: The emoji is an artefact of the browser session's tab-title handling, not the site. The raw HTML has a genuinely empty <title></title>, so the substance of the finding (no service or town text in any page title, no meta description) stands, but it is an empty title rather than an emoji one.
